s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Purulent discharge for 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of right upper eyelid swelling
10 months of purulent discharge
No history of trauma to the head
No symptoms of fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node measures 11 × 7 mm
MRI shows high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT shows opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction
Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: MRI and CT findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus

shortlist.label: Ethmoid sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings of opacification and expansion of the right ethmoid sinus

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge

shortlist.label: Pott's puffy tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid with purulent discharge

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic infection with purulent discharge and absence of bone destruction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a 2-year history of swelling of her right upper eyelid with purulent discharge, along with imaging studies showing opacification and expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses, and histopathology revealing mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, is most consistent with Pott's puffy tumor, a rare complication of frontal sinusitis.

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: While mucoceles can cause expansion of sinuses, the presence of purulent discharge and inflammatory infiltrate suggests an infectious process like Pott's puffy tumor.

rejected.label: Ethmoid sinus mucocele
rejected.why: The primary involvement of the frontal sinus and the clinical presentation make ethmoid sinus mucocele less likely.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the lacrimal sac and would not explain the sinus opacification and expansion seen on imaging.

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: While actinomycosis can cause chronic infection, the specific findings of sinus opacification, expansion, and the nature of the discharge are more characteristic of Pott's puffy tumor.
